hosts.browser: headless Google Chrome on this Mac, OfflineAudioContext
hosts.ios: iPhone 17 Pro simulator, iOS 26.5, React Native 0.86.3, React Native Audio API 0.13.3, Release, OfflineAudioContext
hosts.android: emulator AVD dosekeep_api35 (API 35, arm64-v8a), same React Native / Audio API versions, Release APK

delayChain.expected: impulses 1, 0.5, 0.25, 0.125 at frames 0, D, 2D, 3D (D = 441 at 44.1 kHz, 480 at 48 kHz)
delayChain.reading: On both native hosts the output contains a single impulse at frame 0 whose value equals one tap gain (0.5^3 on iOS; 0.5^2 or 0.5^1 on Android, differing between the two Android renders of the same fixture). The dry path (gain 1 at frame 0) and the delayed taps are absent. This is consistent with the host keeping only part of the fan-out/fan-in graph and applying no delay, but the topology has not been isolated yet; the Android repeat mismatch also shows nondeterministic offline rendering for this graph.

convolverIdentity.expected: single impulse through ConvolverNode(normalize=false) reproduces the seeded 0.25 s stereo response
convolverIdentity.reading: Native output is repeatable and identical between iOS and Android, has RMS within 0.2% of the response and peak about 1% higher, but deviates from the response by up to 4.7% of full scale. The host convolver therefore does not reproduce the impulse response sample-for-sample; the deviation pattern (scale, lag, or channel handling) is not yet isolated.

unchanged: timing (raw fail at 44.1 kHz, adapter-scheduled pass), filter, pan and HRTF results are the same as the fixture-version-3 runs on all three hosts.
interpretation: TuneJS delay and reverb effects are verified only on the browser host. React Native Audio API 0.13.3 does not pass the delay-chain or convolver-identity fixtures in OfflineAudioContext on either platform, so native effect parity is an open host gate rather than a TuneJS bug. Next step: topology-isolating fixtures (single delay, source fan-out, destination fan-in) and a convolver fit diagnostic before deciding between an upstream fix, a TuneJS-owned DSP path, or a documented native limitation.
